name: Duvakitug
summary: Duvakitug (TEV-'574) is an anti-TL1A antibody co-developed with Teva, with IV induction and subcutaneous maintenance in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. Sanofi leads a four-study Phase 3 programme: UC induction NCT07184996 (primary completion 2028-05) and maintenance NCT07185009 (2028-09), CD induction NCT07184931 (2029-05) and maintenance NCT07184944 (2029-08), after the RELIEVE UCCD Phase 2b met its primary endpoints in both diseases (Sanofi release 2024-12-17). Price anchor: Humira at $57,982 per Medicare Part D beneficiary in 2024, the comparator the book's other anti-TL1A (tulisokibart) uses. Uptake anchor: tulisokibart's seeded peaks (0.05 UC, 0.06 CD, half of what upadacitinib and the IL-23s measurably took) and Zeposia's fitted UC launch curve, reused. Sanofi keeps half: profits and losses in major markets are shared equally with Teva.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07185009 and NCT07184944 (ClinicalTrials.gov): separate maintenance studies after induction, the same IV-induction, SC-maintenance design as the tulisokibart seed
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT07185009 is a maintenance study (primary outcome 'Pivotal Maintenance Sub-Study Cohort 1: clinical remission by mMS') and NCT07184944 is titled a maintenance study; separate induction studies NCT07184996/NCT07184931. Chronic maintenance dosing holds.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Humira: CMS Part D 2024, 'Humira (2 presentations)', $906,310,362 over 15,631 beneficiaries = $57,982 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator: Humira is the anchor the book's tulisokibart seed uses (self-injected antibody labelled in both UC and CD), kept so the two anti-TL1As price alike. Discrepancy to flag: the tulisokibart seed quotes Humira at $53,401 ($208.9mm over 3,912 beneficiaries), which does not match the book's current demand table; this uses the current table. Case against: Skyrizi, the newest mechanism labelled in both UC and CD with the same IV-induction, SC-maintenance design, reads $66,409 (Part D 2024), 15% higher; Rinvoq reads $47,673. Humira's Medicare spend is mostly rheumatology and dermatology use, and its price now faces biosimilar pressure
list_price_per_patient.check: Re-ran lookup.py demand Humira: Part D 2024 'Humira (2 presentations)' $906,310,362.16 / 15,631 = $57,982 (0.057982 mm USD). Units right. Also re-ran Skyrizi Part D 2024 $66,409 and Rinvoq $47,673; both match the note. The researcher's flagged discrepancy holds: drug_demand carries no Humira row giving $208.9mm over 3,912 beneficiaries, so the tulisokibart seed's $53,401 is not reproducible from the current table (separate fix for that seed). Comparator choice remains a judgement.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention: halving a CMS per-beneficiary figure lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices (backend/gross_to_net.py; same value in the tulisokibart seed)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Net is 50% of list. A competitive, heavily rebated IBD class supports a large discount
gross_to_net_pct.check: Direction checked: 0.5 is share OFF list, net = 50% of list; matches house convention and the tulisokibart seed row (lookup.py seed tulisokibart, 'share off list').

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the stock per year
discontinuation_pct.source: reused from the tulisokibart seed: Dulai PS et al., Crohn's & Colitis 360, 2026 (IQVIA PharMetrics Plus, 6,726 US adults with UC starting an advanced therapy): 38.1% still on first advanced therapy at 36 months, so 27.5% of the stock stops each year
discontinuation_pct.note: Same class, same disease. Case against: measured in UC only, and first-line persistence; Crohn's persistence may differ
discontinuation_pct.check: tulisokibart seed row quotes Dulai PS et al. 38.1% on first advanced therapy at 36 months; 1 - 0.381^(1/3) = 0.275. Arithmetic holds and matches the seed value.

forecast_start_year.source: ClinicalTrials.gov primary completion dates (context file): UC induction NCT07184996 2028-05-09, UC maintenance NCT07185009 2028-09-21
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT. No launch date is published by Sanofi or Teva (searched). UC maintenance reads out in late 2028, a BLA follows around the turn of 2029, and a standard 12-month review puts approval around early 2030, so 2030 is the first year of revenue. Case against: any slip in filing or review makes it 2031, and Crohn's (maintenance 2029-08) comes about a year later
forecast_start_year.check: Primary completion dates 2028-05-09 (NCT07184996) and 2028-09-21 (NCT07185009) confirmed in the context file and book trials table. 2030 follows the same PCD-to-revenue lag the tulisokibart seed uses (PCD 2026-08 -> revenue 2028). Remains a judgement.

exus_multiple.source: Dupixent, Sanofi FY2025 20-F (0001628280-26-008403), in the book's asset_revenue_regions: US EUR 11,538mm, Europe EUR 1,957mm, rest of world EUR 2,219mm. (1,957 + 2,219) / 11,538 = 0.362
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT. Sanofi's own chronic immunology biologic; Sanofi has no IBD product to read a split from. Case against: IBD biologics tend to sell relatively more outside the US than Dupixent (Europe has high IBD prevalence), so this may understate ex-US; AbbVie's Skyrizi reads lower at 0.155 (book's lutikizumab seed). Also, Teva leads commercialisation in Europe, Israel and specified countries, and markets outside the 'major markets' are on a royalty, which economics_share does not capture
exus_multiple.check: book asset_revenue_regions, Dupilumab FY2025: US EUR 11,538mm (sec_fsds and annual report table 0001628280-26-008403), Europe 1,957mm, Rest of the world 2,219mm. (1,957+2,219)/11,538 = 0.3619. Skyrizi comparison also checked: International 2,360 / US 15,202 = 0.155 (AbbVie 0001551152-26-000008). Judgement on comparator stands.

economics_share.source: Teva FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-034532) and Sanofi/Teva release 2023-10-04 (sanofi.com/en/media-room/press-releases/2023/2023-10-04-05-00-00-2754288), also described in Sanofi's FY2023 20-F (0001121404-24-000009): 'each company will equally share the remaining development costs globally and net profits and losses in major markets, with other markets subject to a royalty arrangement'. Sanofi paid $500mm upfront with up to $1bn in milestones
economics_share.note: 0.5 is exact for the major markets, which carry most of the value. Minor markets run on a royalty (Sanofi receives or pays depending on who leads there), not modelled. Milestone payments to Teva of up to $1bn are not in this field
economics_share.check: Sanofi release 2023-10-04 (sanofi.com/en/media-room/press-releases/2023/2023-10-04-05-00-00-2754288) and Teva 8-K EX-99.1 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/818686/000119312523250305/d547410dex991.htm): 'each company will equally share the development costs globally and net profits and losses in major markets, with other markets subject to a royalty arrangement'; $500mm (EUR 469mm) upfront, up to $1bn milestones; Teva leads commercialisation in Europe, Israel and specified other countries, Sanofi in North America, Japan, other Asia and rest of world. 50/50 holds for major markets. Minor wording note: the release says 'development costs', not 'remaining development costs'. The Teva 10-K and Sanofi 20-F accessions quoted were not independently opened; the release and Teva 8-K carry the term.

eligible_pct.source: reused from the tulisokibart seed: Xu F et al. (CDC), Journal of Investigative Medicine 2022;70:1771-1776: 13.6% of 52,280 US UC patients were prescribed a biologic in 2019
eligible_pct.note: The label will be moderately to severely active UC, the pool that reaches advanced therapy; kept equal to tulisokibart so the two TL1As share one pool. Case against: 2019 data understate today's advanced-therapy use, which has grown with JAKs and S1Ps
eligible_pct.check: tulisokibart seed row: Xu F et al. (CDC) J Investig Med 2022, 13.6% of 52,280 UC patients prescribed a biologic in 2019; value matches.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: reused from the tulisokibart seed: set against upadacitinib, which held 12.1% of UC patients on advanced therapy in Q2 2025, its fourth year (Singh S et al., Journal of Crohn's and Colitis 2025, 71 US health systems); the engine needs 0.101 to match that, and 0.05 reaches half
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: 0.5x upadacitinib, the multiple the tulisokibart seed chose. Case for higher: Phase 2b placebo-adjusted remission was among the strongest in class (Sanofi 2024-12-17). Case for lower: duvakitug is likely second to market behind tulisokibart (Merck, readout 2026) and competes with Roche's afimkibart in the same class, so one TL1A share may be split three ways
penetration_peak_pct.check: tulisokibart seed row: upadacitinib 12.1% of UC advanced-therapy patients Q2 2025 (Singh S et al., JCC 2025), engine needs 0.101, 0.05 is half. Value and reasoning match; 0.5x multiple is a judgement.

ramp_steepness.note: The only UC-labelled launch on file whose series reaches an inflection
ramp_steepness.check: Zeposia Part D beneficiaries re-read via lookup.py demand Zeposia: 104, 406, 655, 1,034, 1,271 (2020-2024), as the seed states; k 1.005 matches the tulisokibart seed.

ramp_midpoint_year.check: Matches the tulisokibart UC seed row, 2.15 years.
